label: rem:sign-sequence-of-braid-invariant
title: The sign-sequence functor as a transfinite refinement of the crossing number
html:
A surreal number x \in \mathbf{No} admits a canonical sign-sequence presentation: a function s_x : \alpha \to \{+, -\} for some ordinal \alpha = b(x). The sequence encodes Conway's \{L \mid R\} construction step-by-step: at stage \beta < \alpha, s_x(\beta) = + means "x is the rightmost option", and s_x(\beta) = - means "leftmost option". Hecke generators have two eigenvalues, q (symmetric channel) and -q^{-1} (antisymmetric channel) (Hoefsmit seminormal form). This binary choice at each level is exactly the sign-sequence data, providing a canonical functor from braid words to surreals.

The sign sequence has length equal to the crossing number c(\beta), so b(\mathrm{surr}(\beta, t)) \leq c(\beta). Equality holds when the braid is reduced. This cleanly refines the crossing-number invariant by an ordinal-valued quantity.

The sign sequence carries strictly more information than the crossing number: it records which eigenchannel is chosen at each crossing. Distinct braids with the same crossing number generally give distinct surreals. Surrealisation is a stronger braid invariant valued in \mathbf{No} / \sim. It is the precise sense in which "Hoefsmit seminormal form is the surreal \{L \mid R\} construction". It refines the Jones polynomial (Jones polynomial birthday refinement) and places knot complexity on a transfinite scale.
